- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weakly positive or negative (e.g., <0.4 or <0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged price spikes are often overcorrected in the model; model tends to peak too early and then drop too sharply.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high prices longer than observed, especially after strong upward moves.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates the first 5–7 days after a spike, then gradually converges — adjust downward in early horizon.
- When sentiment is rising but prices are flat or slightly falling, model often misreads momentum and overreacts.
- Model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven corrections — when sentiment shifts sharply, model lags in adjusting price trajectory.
